title: Maple-Preview bets on fast ternary reasoning for personal devices
friendlyTitle: A fast open model aims to bring reasoning to personal devices
summary: DeepGrove unveiled Maple-Preview, an open-source 20B mixture-of-experts reasoning model with ternary weights and 1.49B active parameters. Its model card reports a 5.31 GB checkpoint, a 131K context window, and more than 200 tokens per second on an M4 Mac mini.
friendlySummary: Maple-Preview uses a very efficient number format to run quickly on Apple computers and even an iPhone. It is open source but still an early preview.
whyItMatters: Ultra-low-precision models could bring fast reasoning and private personalization to consumer hardware. This remains a preview with limited agent training, so its striking speed and benchmark results should be treated as promising evidence rather than a finished general-purpose assistant.
friendlyWhyItMatters: Fast local models could give you more private and personal AI without sending every task to the cloud.
